claim: Let \(G=(A,B;E)\) be a finite simple bipartite graph with a fixed proper edge-colouring. If \(\deg_G(a)\ge 3\) for every \(a\in A\), then the edges of \(G\) admit a global total order such that the incident-colour sequences at the endpoints of every edge are distinct. Consequently, every finite simple \(d\)-regular bipartite graph is sequentially orderable under every proper edge-colouring for every integer \(d\ge 3\).
integrity: The universal theorem is proved deductively. The embedded exhaustive computation is only a finite regression test of the construction and is not used as an infinite proof. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The theorem does not settle nonbipartite regular graphs of degrees \(3,4,5\). Simplicity and proper edge-colouring are essential to the proof as written, and degree \(2\) has genuine bipartite counterexamples. Direct public full-text retrieval of arXiv:2609.11832 was unavailable during comparison, leaving a residual bibliographic risk of an unindexed body-only observation.
title: A one-sided block criterion for bipartite sequential orderability
